Protection that reports — and closes the screen

While you are armed, Shieldra watches the SIM, the phone\'s motion and wrong unlock attempts. When one fires, it records the event and alerts your own channels — with the position and a photo when the phone can produce them. A confirmed lift outside a safe zone is treated as a snatch: the screen closes at once, and the phone asks for your proof for ten minutes before it escalates. The device admin it asks for holds two powers only: notice a wrong unlock, and close the screen after that snatch. It can never reset your password or wipe the phone.

How to get an app password

An app password is not your normal password. Gmail: turn on 2-Step Verification, then open myaccount.google.com/apppasswords, create one for \"Mail\", and paste the 16 letters here. Outlook and Yahoo have the same option in their account security settings. The server fields fill in automatically for Gmail, Outlook, Yahoo and iCloud.
Telegram alerts are part of Shieldra Pro. On the free plan alerts go by email only. Tap to see Pro.
How to get the bot token and chat ID

1) In Telegram, open @BotFather, send /newbot, follow the steps, and copy the token it gives you. 2) Open your new bot and send it any message. 3) Open @userinfobot and it replies with your chat ID — paste that number here.

Camera and microphone: evidence after an incident. Location: where the phone is. Notifications: to keep protection running and show alerts. Device admin: watch a wrong unlock attempt — nothing else. Screen lock: to confirm it is you for export, deletion and app lock.

Export evidence as an encrypted file, delete it automatically after 90 days (events) and 30 days (evidence), lock the app with your screen lock, or delete all data now in Settings. Uninstalling Shieldra removes everything it stored.
My phone is stolen — what do I do?

Work through this from another device — a laptop or a friend\'s phone. The order keeps the most: lock the handset, take its position, see who holds it, change your numbers, and leave any wipe to last, because a wipe destroys the evidence stored on the phone itself.
Lock it with Google\'s own Find My Device

Open android.com/find in a browser and sign in with the Google account on the stolen phone, then lock it there with a message and a contact number for whoever finds it. That works even if Shieldra is not running. Shieldra cannot lock the screen on demand; it closes the screen by itself only after a confirmed snatch, and it cannot wipe the device either.
Ask where it is, from your own Telegram chat

Send /locate and the phone answers with one map pin; /track on keeps sending one at your tracking interval until you send /track off. It answers only while protection is armed, \"Control from Telegram\" is on in Protection settings, your plan is Premium and the phone has a network. Commands are not queued: if the phone was offline, send it again.

Send /photo and the phone takes one front-camera picture and replies with it. Any alert that already fired — panic, failed unlocks, a SIM change, motion — carried a photo and a position of its own when the camera and the GPS could produce one, so read your chat history before you ask for anything new.
Make it loud, and say it is lost

/alarm sounds the siren until you send /stopalarm. /lost puts your own message and contact number on the screen for a finder, and /found clears it. /status replies with the battery, the network and whether the guards are armed.
Block the handset and file a report

Your carrier can blacklist the IMEI so the phone cannot join any mobile network, and the police report needs the same number. The IMEI is printed on the box and on the SIM tray, and shown by Settings › About phone on the device.
Change what the phone can open
From another device, change your Google password first, then email, banking and messaging. A phone that is unlocked in someone else\'s hands is a key to the codes that reset those accounts.
Erase only when the data matters more than the evidence

Erase from android.com/find. It removes everything on the phone, including the events, photos and recordings Shieldra stored there, and nothing on the handset can be recovered afterwards. Do it once the position and the photos you need are safe in your Telegram chat or your mailbox.
The only copy that is not on the phone

Shieldra has no server and no account of its own, so everything it recorded lives on the stolen handset. The copy outside it is what its alerts already delivered — to the Telegram bot you created and the mailbox you configured. Those messages carry the time, the battery, a map link and a photo when one could be taken, and they survive a wipe because they already left.
What Shieldra cannot do for you

It cannot wipe the device or read anyone\'s PIN, and it cannot lock the screen on demand. It cannot locate a phone that is switched off or has no network, it does not queue your commands, and it never reports a position it did not measure. A factory reset, an uninstall or clearing the app storage removes what it kept on the handset.
Keep Shieldra alive on this phone

On this phone\'s software the guards are usually stopped by the battery manager, not by a thief. These switches live in the phone\'s own menus, and none of them has a link that opens it, so each one is written out with its menu names. Copy a line and search for it in Settings if your build words it differently.

Settings › Apps › App management › Shieldra › Battery usage › Allow background activity
Do not pause it when unused
An armed protection app spends its life unused — that is the point of it. This setting puts such an app to sleep after a quiet spell.
Settings › Apps › App management › Shieldra › Pause app activity if unused › Off
Keep it out of the quick freeze
The freeze list suspends apps the system believes nobody is using, and a suspended service stamps no check and sends no alert.
Settings › Battery › Advanced settings › App quick freeze › Shieldra › Off

Settings › Battery › Power saving mode › Off

This is the one switch Shieldra can hand you: the \"Keep running — ignore battery saver\" row in Protection settings opens the system prompt for it.

Keep it out of the cleaner
The one-tap speed-up force-stops every app it considers idle, and a force-stop is not something a service survives or reports.
Phone Manager › Speed up › exclude Shieldra

Before you pay for protection, know what the phone already does by itself. Android ships theft features of its own, and they are good ones. This screen names them plainly and then says, in one card, the single thing this app puts on top of them.

On newer Android versions the phone watches its own motion sensors for the shape of a snatch — being torn from your hand or pulled off a table — and locks the screen by itself. It needs no network and no SIM change to do it. It locks; it does not say where the phone went.

If a run of wrong PINs or passwords is entered inside a short window, the phone locks itself and stops accepting the screen lock until the owner signs in to their Google account. A thief pressing at the keypad is stopped, and the owner is not told.

When the phone is not confident it is you, it refuses sensitive changes: turning off Find My Device, changing or removing the screen lock. From a browser you can lock the phone and sign it out of the account. The intruder is slowed down; nothing is gathered about them.

On hardware that supports it, the phone can still be found after it has been switched off, by letting nearby phones hear it over Bluetooth and report what they heard. This is a real answer to the oldest trick in the book: powering the phone down.

Android puts a growing wait on the keypad after repeated failures, and a device that has been given the right to erase itself can wipe on a run of failures. That erase is an administrator power: Shieldra does not hold it, so Shieldra never wipes your phone — the erase it offers is the one you choose yourself.

The phone\'s own finder shows a position on a map, makes it ring, locks it and erases it. It belongs to the account the phone is signed in to, so it speaks to that account\'s service and not to a channel of your choosing.

Every feature above is about stopping the phone from being used. One thing is missing from all of them: a record of what happened, made on the phone and sent to you. When the SIM is pulled or the phone is lifted after sitting still, Shieldra writes the event down, takes a front-camera photo, and sends you a message with the position it measured and the battery it read — into your own Telegram and your own email, not into a service it runs. And a patrol outside the service tells you when the guards have gone quiet, which is the failure no phone reports by itself.

These are Google\'s names for Google\'s features, and makers rename them and ship them on different versions. Nothing on this screen was checked on your phone: the Health screen is the only view in this app that reports what was actually measured here.
